To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of dissipated kinetic, strain, magnetic and electric energy for magnetoelastodynamic waves propagating in a homogeneous and isotropically elastic medium with finite electric conductivity is proportional to the square of the wave number and inversely proportional to the square root of the electric conductivity.
the dissipation of energy for the case of finite electric conductivity is identical with the corresponding rate of dissipation for the case of thermal coupling.

(a) the characteristic roots of the governing equations of motion are obtained in their canonical form, (b) the rate of dissipated energy for magnetoelatic waves coincides with that of thermoelastic waves, (c) the dissipation rate is proportional to the square root of the electric conductivity, and (d) the dissipation is independent of the magnetic field intensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the propagation and the dissipation of elastic waves in an elastic medium that is coupled to an electrically conducting medium.
the propagation of magnitoelastic waves in an elastic medium exhibiting finite conductivity.
the propagation of elastic and electromagnetic waves within a homogeneous, isotropic and conductive medium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dissipation of energy for a conductive elastic medium is the same as that of the corresponding thermoelastic medium.
the finite conductivity effects upon the propagation of magneteoelastic waves are analogous to those of thermal coupling upon the propagation of thermoelastic waves.
the rate of dissipated energy for a magnetoelastic wave is proportional to the square of the wave number and the square of the time variable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a complete analysis of the propagation of magnetonelastic waves within a conductive medium, and we have established the rate of dissipating energy of these waves as they propagate through the medium.
the dissipation of energy for the magnetoelastic wave is governed by the same rate as for the thermoelastic wave.
the dissipation of energy for elastic waves is a function of the elastic and the magnetic properties of the medium and the frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the presence of electric conductivity, there is a finite rate at which the energy of magnetoelastic disturbances dissipates as time progresses.
the dissipation of energy is independent of the electric conductivity of the medium.
the rate of dissipated energy is a function of the wave number and the frequency.
